bandReport.notes:
Band covers items 14-32 whole. Item 14 opens p10 c1 with its full stem and item 32 closes p16 c2 with all four options, so nothing spills past either edge.

DIRECTIONS BLOCKS AND PASSAGE MAPPING. Two blocks fall in this band.

Block 1 (p12 c1, top) reads 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items : Read the following three passages and answer the items that follow the passages. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.' It covers items 21-23 and carries THREE passages, each governing exactly ONE item: Passage-1 (city pollution / odd-even scheme, p12 c1) governs item 21; Passage-2 (good corporate governance, p12 c2) governs item 22; Passage-3 (elephants as landscape architects, p14 c1) governs item 23. Each of those three contexts is therefore used by a single item and will raise a lonely-context warning at merge. That is the LEGITIMATE case the warning names - a directions block giving each item its own passage - not per-item material parked in context and not a lost sibling at a band seam. The block is fully contained in this band (3 items, 3 passages, all four columns read), so there is no sibling elsewhere.

Block 2 (p16 c1, top) reads 'Directions for the following 5 (five) items : Read the following three passages and answer the items that follow the passages. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.' It covers items 31-35, of which only 31 and 32 fall in this band. Its Passage-1 (segregation of municipal waste / waste-to-energy, p16 c1) governs BOTH item 31 and item 32, and both carry it byte-identically so they group as one set. Its Passage-2 (organic farming / farmyard manure / atropine) BEGINS at the foot of p16 c2 and its items are on p18, which is the next band - I own no item under it, so it is deliberately not transcribed here. Items 33-35 and Passage-3 of this block belong to the next band.

No 'Directions for the following N items' preamble and no 'Passage - N' label is inside any context; contexts hold passage prose only.

COLUMN CROPS - two pages mis-split, both recoverable. p10: the c2 crop starts to the RIGHT of the item numbers, so '17.', '18.', '19.' and '20.' are missing from the top-left of p10-c2 and instead run down the right edge of p10-c1. p14: identical defect, '26.' through '30.' sit on the right edge of p14-c1 rather than in p14-c2. In both cases the item BODIES are complete in c2 and only the numerals were displaced; numbering was confirmed by reading p10.png and p14.png, where the vertical alignment of each stray numeral against its c2 item is unambiguous. p12 and p16 split cleanly (their c2 crops carry '22.' and '32.' correctly).

VERBATIM ODDITIES PRESERVED. Passage-1 of block 1 prints the decimal with a middle dot, 'PM 2.5' set as 'PM 2·5'; the middle dot is transcribed as printed. The same passage sets CO2 and NOx with true subscripts; they are written as \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{NO_x}\). Item 22 opens 'Which of the following statements best reflects' where items 21, 23 and 32 open 'Which one of the following statements best reflects'; transcribed exactly as printed. Item 24 uses the circled-plus operator, verified at magnification to be ⊕ and not a plain plus or an asterisk; written as \oplus.

COLLISION CHECK. Items 14, 20 and 31 share the same four options (1 only / 2 only / Both 1 and 2 / Neither 1 nor 2). Their numbered statement lists are kept in the STEM, so the three stems differ and their content hashes cannot collide. Items 31 and 32 share a context but have entirely different stems and options.

SUBTOPIC WARNING. Item 14 (parity of a signed sum of five integers, three even and two odd) has no good catalog match; filed under Basic Numeracy / Number System with the ad-hoc subtopic 'Odd and Even Numbers'.

No defective questions, no duplicate options, no skipped numbers; 14 through 32 are consecutive and each appears exactly once.

questions.stem:
Three of the five positive integers p, q, r, s, t are even and two of them are odd (not necessarily in order). Consider the following :
1. \(p + q + r - s - t\) is definitely even.
2. \(2p + q + 2r - 2s + t\) is definitely odd.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?

questions.context: To tackle the problem of pollution in cities, policy makers think that drastic actions like temporary use of odd-even number scheme for vehicles, closing schools, factories, construction activities, and banning the use of certain type of vehicles are a way forward. Even then the air is not clean. Vehicles more than 15 years old comprise one percent of the total; and taking them off the road will not make any difference. Banning certain fuels and car types arbitrarily is not proper. Diesel engines produce more PM 2·5 and less \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) than petrol or CNG engines. On the other hand, both diesel and CNG engines produce more \(\mathrm{NO_x}\) than petrol engines. No one has measured the amount of \(\mathrm{NO_x}\) that CNG engines are emitting. Arbitrary bans on vehicles that have passed mandated fitness tests and periodic pollution tests are unfair. What is needed is the scientific and reliable information about the source of pollutants on a continuing basis and the technologies that will work to reduce pollution from them.

questions.context: Good corporate governance structures encourage companies to provide accountability and control. Effective corporate governance enhances access to external financing by firms, leading to greater investment, higher growth and employment. Investors look to place their funds where the standards of disclosure, of timely and accurate financial reporting, and of equal treatment to all stakeholders are met.

questions.context: Elephants are landscape architects, creating clearings in the forest, preventing overgrowth of certain plant species and allowing space for the regeneration of others, which in turn provide sustenance to other herbivorous animals. Elephant dung provides nourishment to plants and animals and acts as a breeding ground for insects. In times of drought, they access water by digging holes which benefits other wildlife.

questions.context: In India, the segregation of municipal waste at source is rare. Recycling is mostly with the informal sector. More than three-fourths of the municipal budget goes into collection and transportation, which leaves very little for processing/resource recovery and disposal. Where does waste-to-energy fit into all this ? Ideally it fits in the chain after segregation (between wet waste and the rest), collection, recycling, and before getting to the landfill. Which technology is most appropriate in converting waste to energy depends on what is in the waste (that is biodegradable versus non-biodegradable component) and its calorific value. The biodegradable component of India's municipal solid waste is a little over 50 per cent, and biomethanation offers a major solution for processing this.
questions.stem:

1. Collection, processing and segregation of municipal waste should be with government agencies.
2. Resource recovery and recycling require technological inputs that can be best handled by private sector enterprises.
Which of the assumptions given above is/are correct ?
